I see the to_cents function truncates floats instead of rounding, which can cause off-by-one cent errors. I should switch to using Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP for converting amounts to cents, keeping it consistent with the half-up rounding used elsewhere.

I verify this against the discount and tax test cases, confirming the expected cent calculations match, then check report.py for other callers of to_cents that might be affected.
Found it: `to_cents` truncates floats instead of rounding, so `19.99 * 100` becomes 1998 instead of 1999. I'll fix it with decimal-exact half-up rounding, consistent with `discounts.py`/`tax.py`.

content.text:
The bug was in `ledger/currency.py`, not in the totals code. `to_cents` converted dollars to cents with `int(amount * 100)`, which cuts off the decimals instead of rounding. In binary floating point, `19.99 * 100` comes out as `1998.9999…`, so it became `1998` cents instead of `1999`. The same thing hit `0.29` and `4.35`.

I changed `to_cents` to do the conversion with `Decimal(str(amount))` and round half up. That makes it exact, and it uses the same half-up rounding as `discounts.py` and `tax.py`. Its only caller is `Line.cents()`, so I didn't need to change anything else.

The full suite now passes: 5 tests, including all 4 in `tests/test_totals.py`.
